zh.simulation: 教学模型 · 不运行真实 Agent 或外部命令
zh.codeNote: 下方为源码节选或明确标注的设计概括；交互情境均为教学示意。
zh.fallback: 启用 JavaScript 可操作图解；静态图、结论和来源无需 JavaScript。
zh.title: 外部消息如何影响执行设备？
zh.lead: 追踪不可信输入到工具执行的路径，比较权限约束与不暴露凭据分别解决什么。
zh.diagramLabel: 不可信消息、Agent、工具权限与设备之间的影响路径
zh.injection: 情境：输入试图改变任务
zh.credential: 情境：正常调用暴露凭据
zh.restrict: 限制端点工具权限（防护设计示意）
zh.opaque: 凭据由工具使用，模型看不到原值（设计示意）
zh.endpoint: 执行设备 / 返回结果
zh.sourceText: 外部评论夹带与登录修复无关的操作要求。此处不含可执行攻击载荷。
zh.credentialText: 任务需要合法调用服务；工具的结果可能意外包含演示凭据 DEMO_SECRET。
zh.loopBad: ! 教学假设：模型误把外部内容当成指令
zh.toolAllowed: ! 缺少约束时，操作可能到达设备
zh.legitAllowed: ✓ 允许完成任务所需的服务操作
zh.endpointRisk: ! 设备和私有数据可能受影响
zh.secretHidden: ✓ 模型只收到操作结果，不收到凭据原值
zh.partial: 限制执行权限与隔离凭据解决不同风险；任何单个开关都不是完整安全保证。
zh.caption: 外部事件扩大输入面，远端 daemon 扩大执行影响范围；安全需要在实际权限与工具返回边界上建立约束。
zh.limit0: 这里是安全的本地状态模拟；不执行命令、不读取秘密，也不向任何服务发送数据。
zh.limit1: 两个防护开关是为了说明风险边界的设计示例，不是原文已证明或原型已实现的安全机制。
zh.limit2: 提示模型“不要泄露”不是权限隔离；身份、授权、审计和端点互信仍需具体设计和验证。
zh.question: 模型看不到凭据原值，是否就不能滥用已授权工具？
zh.answer: 仍可能。不暴露凭据保护秘密可见性；工具权限还需限制模型能够执行的动作及影响范围。
zh.step0Title: 把外部资料当作不可信输入
zh.step0Explanation: 事件驱动会读取更多环境内容；被允许监听不代表内容本身可信。
zh.step1Title: 追踪模型如何选择动作
zh.step1Explanation: 此情境假设模型可能受骗，用来检查后续边界；不是声称所有输入都能成功注入。
zh.step2Explanation: 限制执行范围可以阻断本条越权路径；合法调用仍可能返回敏感信息。
zh.step3Title: 检查动作影响与返回信息
zh.step3Explanation: 切换凭据开关，观察合法任务中的信息可见性。没有云端入侵，也可能发生凭据暴露。
zh.source1: 文章 §8.4：尚待解决的安全与隐私

en.simulation: Teaching model · No real agents or external commands
en.codeNote: Below: source excerpts or explicitly labeled design summaries. Interactive scenarios are illustrative.
en.fallback: Enable JavaScript to operate the figure. The static diagram, conclusion, and sources work without it.
en.title: How can an external message affect execution devices?
en.lead: Trace untrusted input to tool execution and compare what permission constraints and opaque credential use each address.
en.diagramLabel: An influence path through untrusted input, the agent, tool permissions, and a device
en.injection: Scenario: input tries to redirect work
en.credential: Scenario: a normal call exposes credentials
en.opaque: Tools use credentials without revealing their values (design example)
en.sourceText: An external comment includes an instruction unrelated to the login fix. No executable attack payload is included.
en.credentialText: Work needs a legitimate service call; its output may accidentally contain the fictional credential DEMO_SECRET.
en.loopBad: ! Teaching assumption: the model mistakes external content for an instruction
en.toolBlocked: ■ Tool layer refuses an out-of-scope operation
en.toolAllowed: ! Without constraints, the operation may reach the device
en.legitAllowed: ✓ Allow the service operation needed for the task
en.endpoint0: … Device has not received an operation
en.endpointRisk: ! The device and private data may be affected
en.secretHidden: ✓ The model receives the operation result without the credential value
en.partial: Permission constraints and credential isolation address different risks. Neither switch guarantees complete security.
en.caption: External events expand the input surface; remote daemons expand execution reach. Controls must exist at real permission and tool-output boundaries.
en.limit0: This is a local state simulation. It executes no command, reads no secret, and sends no data to any service.
en.limit1: The two switches are design examples illustrating boundaries, not protections established by the article or implemented by the prototype.
en.limit2: Telling a model not to leak is not permission isolation. Identity, authorization, auditing, and endpoint trust need concrete design and validation.
en.question: If a model cannot see credentials, can it still misuse an authorized tool?
en.answer: It may still misuse a tool. Hiding credentials protects secret visibility; tool permissions must also constrain actions and their scope.
en.step0Title: Treat external material as untrusted input
en.step0Explanation: Event-driven systems read more environmental content. Permission to listen does not make the content trustworthy.
en.step1Title: Trace how an action is selected
en.step1Explanation: The scenario assumes the model can be misled to examine later boundaries. It does not claim every input succeeds at injection.
en.step2Title: Enforce constraints at the tool boundary
en.step2Explanation: A scope constraint can block this out-of-scope path. A legitimate call may still return sensitive information.
en.step3Title: Check both action impact and returned information
en.step3Explanation: Toggle credential handling to inspect visibility during legitimate work. Exposure can happen even without a cloud compromise.
